label: copy phase: re-fed b whose next output is 0 (or b), in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the fed-back input is b (100% of activations), and almost always when the token about to be output is 0 (~67% of mass, the bigram b0 in the original) or b (~29%, the bigram bb). It does not fire in the original or delimiter phase, on any input other than b, on the first occurrence of b, or at recall_idx 0-2. Magnitude is largest in long sequences (L=9 holds 64% of mass; none at L<=4) and when b sat early-mid in the original (strongest examples: b at original position 2 followed by 0, L=8-9); more digits in the sequence raises the rate. Precision is low (~15-20%): most b->0 / b->b copy steps in long sequences do not activate, and I found no extra condition that separates them, so this is a sparse, context-gated b-then-0 detector rather than a full explanation.
